source.title: Why neural networks find simple solutions: the many regularizers of geometric complexity
source.authors: Benoit Dherin; M. Munn; M. Rosca; D. G. Barrett

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or text corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies network width and batch size and reports test loss or accuracy, using different architectures and training setups from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, adaptive optimizer comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. It reports GC measurements, but GC is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The ResNet18 width sweep supplies new-setting evidence on V2: test loss decreases again beyond the critical width region. The batch sweeps fix steps rather than epochs and therefore do not test V5's specified budget condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose geometric complexity as a tractable measure controlled by many training heuristics and show that it captures double descent. They present it as a useful lens and performance proxy, rather than establishing a universal predictor or generalization guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ResNet18 width and batch-size sweeps and measures test loss or accuracy alongside geometric complexity. The paper generally uses SGD without momentum and studies heuristics largely in isolation; the listed versions specify other models, datasets, or training conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported geometric-complexity and test-performance relationship varies with learning rate and batch size; under Adam, the batch-size relationship is described as ambiguous. The paper also reports experiments with momentum, augmentation, a learning-rate schedule, and explicit regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches produce higher test accuracy in fixed-step SGD experiments, including the combined schedule, augmentation and L2 setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed number of optimizer updates, smaller batches can improve held-out accuracy in the studied image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning rates are associated with higher test accuracy and lower geometric complexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate choices can jointly affect held-out performance and input-Jacobian geometric complexity.

record.problems: The main experiments use MNIST and CIFAR datasets and DNN or ResNet architectures. Several plotted results are not reported as exact numeric values in the text. The paper notes that the GC estimate in the combined-mechanisms experiments has high variance when computed on small batches. The batch-size experiments hold steps fixed rather than epochs.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional GC and test-performance comparisons for explicit regularization and label noise (Figure 3; Supplementary Material C.3–C.5), plus initialization, momentum, and Adam experiments (Figures 2, 26–35). These do not directly test the listed versions, so they are not separate rows. The Adam batch-size result is described as ambiguous and concerns GC; it does not report a clear test-performance comparison for V5.

untested.parts: Paired natural-label and fixed-random-label fitting and held-out performance. Partial label corruption used as regularization does not supply this comparison.

The original one-hidden-layer architecture, datasets and convergence recipe; classification test error and the precise width at zero training error are not established by the supplied textual results.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance and the contributions of local connectivity or initialization.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD performance under comparable tuning, including recovery through broader tuning or optimizer changes.
Batch-size comparisons with epochs held fixed, and whether adapted recipes remove that penalty. All reported batch sweeps hold steps fixed.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware parameter-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against alternative measures. GC measures input derivatives instead.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Remove the V5 limits_scope verdict: an untested fixed-epoch condition is not evidence that V5 needs qualification. Separate Adam and SGD experiments do not provide a controlled V4 comparison. No exact curve values can be recovered reliably from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, and the specified training recipe. The width sweep uses ResNet18 on CIFAR10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effects of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance and tuning or recovery conditions.
The fixed-epoch comparison and language-model settings. The batch-size sweep uses a fixed number of steps on CIFAR10.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes, architectures, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing the most memorized examples and comparing with random removals.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured train loss, test loss, and geometric complexity.
rows.measure: Test loss as network width increases; authors describe a double-descent curve with a critical region and a second descent.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and 95% confidence interval over three runs; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors state that test loss follows double descent and that after the critical region increased model size leads to decreased GC. The result shows a post-peak decline but includes a test-loss peak near the critical region.
rows.check: The reported second descent supports the post-critical-width effect; the interpolation-region peak does not make that effect partial. Section B.5 says 18 widths but lists 19. Results measure test loss, with no numerical classification-error comparison or exact zero-training-error threshold supplied in the text.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size and tracked test accuracy, training loss, and geometric complexity over training.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; authors state smaller batches yield higher test accuracy and lower GC.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over three runs; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the batch-size association, but the fixed-step setup does not hold the number of epochs fixed.
rows.check: The 100000-step budget gives different epoch budgets across batch sizes, so this row cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch effect. The authors explicitly report higher test accuracy for smaller batches, but exact values are unavailable.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate and tracked test accuracy, training loss, and geometric complexity over training.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; authors state higher learning rates yield higher test accuracy and lower GC.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over three runs; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The learning-rate comparison is not one of the listed claim versions.
rows.check: The learning-rate association is reported explicitly but measures none of the listed versions; observed is not an applicable version-relative state.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size with cosine learning-rate schedule, random-flip augmentation, and L2 regularization; tracked test accuracy and GC.
rows.measure: Test accuracy; authors state smaller batch size yields higher test accuracy and lower GC.
rows.note: This result reports batch-size behavior with additional training mechanisms, but does not hold epochs fixed.
rows.check: The fixed-step comparison cannot establish V5. Figure 25 reports best test accuracy during training, rather than necessarily final accuracy; the row should specify this selection.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR10, widths beyond the critical region, trained with SGD for 100000 steps
relationships.reason: R1 and Section 6 explicitly report a second descent in test loss as width increases beyond the critical region; this supports the widening trend using loss as the held-out measure.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decline in test loss beyond the critical width region remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
